item.title: Bourgain's proof of the circular maximal theorem: an exposition
item.description: arXiv:2609.04471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an exposition of Bourgain's celebrated 1986 proof of the circular maximal theorem.
item.dc:creator: Halit Yigit Gunduz, Jonathan Hickman

item.title: Primes are Complete for a Class of $N$-Bernoulli Convolutions Spectral Pair
item.description: arXiv:2609.04682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the complete number problem for a class of self-similar spectral measures on the real line. For a spectral pair $(\mu,\Lambda)$, a real number $t$ is called complete if $t\Lambda$ is also a spectrum of $\mu$. In this paper we consider the $N$-Bernoulli convolution $\mu_{N^r,\mathcal D},\mathcal D=\{0,1,\ldots,N-1\},$ together with its spectrum $\Lambda_{N^r,N^{r-1}\mathcal D}.$ Our main result establishes that every prime number, apart from certain trivial cases, is complete.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Chao Chi, Jian-Feng Lu, He-Xiang Wang

item.title: On the spectrality of the non-homogeneous golden-mean self-similar measure
item.description: arXiv:2609.04701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the spectral properties of a class of inhomogeneous self-similar measures, which does not admit a non-trivial infinite convolution structure. A central example is the golden-mean self-similar measure $\mu$, for which the existence of an exponential orthonormal basis in the associated $L^2$-space has remained a long-standing open problem. The usual approach for homogeneous self-similar measures does not apply here, new methods are required. We establish several basic properties of the measure and then carry out a detailed numerical study of the zero set of its Fourier transform. Using a scanning and refinement algorithm that combines uniform grid sampling, quadratic interpolation, and golden-section search, we examine a wide range and find no real zeros of $\widehat{\mu}$, which provides concrete evidence that $\mu$ is very likely non-spectral, suggesting that inhomogeneity may serve as a natural obstruction to the existence of exponential orthonormal bases. To the best of our knowledge, our paper is the first attempt to study the spectrality of such measures through a combined analytic and numerical framework.
item.dc:creator: Yi-Qiu Mao, Zhi-Yi Wu

item.title: A Log-Free $n^{1/5}$ Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.05338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite set $S$ of positive integers, put $K(S):=-\min_{x\in\mathbb T}\sum_{s\in S}\cos(2\pi sx)$. Bedert recently proved the uniform lower bound $K(S)\geq |S|^{1/5-o(1)}$. We remove the subpolynomial loss and prove that $K(S)\geq c|S|^{1/5}$ for an absolute constant $c>0$. The proof combines two estimates from Bedert's argument with an exact averaging identity for the asymmetric boundaries of additive intersections. This identity replaces the multiplicative-amplification step responsible for the logarithmic loss.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Shankar

item.title: The weak-type (1,1) bound for the Hardy--Littlewood maximal function is $O(\sqrt{n} \log n)$
item.description: arXiv:2609.05377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal function with respect to Euclidean balls with dimensional dependence $O(\sqrt{n} \log n)$. This improves the order of growth in the classical $O(n)$ estimate of Stein and Str\"omberg. The proof goes through a pointwise bound of the Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator by the heat maximal operator with $\sqrt{n}$ loss. The key technical aspect of our result is an improvement of the weak-type bound for the heat maximal operator from $O(\sqrt{n})$ to $O(\log n)$.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Spector, Cody B. Stockdale

item.title: Asymptotics for the $k$-Hessian Eigenvalue on the Unit Ball
item.description: arXiv:2609.05277v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the limit of the eigenvalue of the $k$-Hessian operator on the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $k\rightarrow \infty$, assuming that the ratio $\frac{n}{k}$ remains fixed. When $n< 2ke$, we moreover identify the limit of the corresponding eigenfunctions. We also derive monotonicity results and consider when the ratio varies in $n$.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas McCleerey, Abhinav Pande, Thidas Wanasinghe

item.title: The convergence of power matrices
item.description: arXiv:2307.13142v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the class of $d\times d$ matrices $B=[b_{i,j}]$ with complex nonzero entries satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^{d}|b_{i,j}|=1$, we provide the conditions for the convergence of power matrices $B^n$ to a nonzero limit matrix.
item.dc:creator: Vyacheslav M. Abramov

item.title: Wavelet and tent space characterizations of $h^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $0 < p \le 1$, with exact $L^2$ convergence, and the maximal class of admissible functions for Goldberg-type splittings
item.description: arXiv:2608.14960v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the wavelet and tent space characterization of the local Hardy space $h^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$ to the full range $0 < p \le 1$. We introduce a local dyadic tent space $t_p$ of coefficient pairs, a father and a mother layer, develop its atomic theory, new for $p < 1$, and prove that membership in $h^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is equivalent to seven conditions: unconditionality of the wavelet expansion, integrability of three wavelet square functions, atomic decompositions, and a Goldberg-type splitting $f - \varphi * f \in H^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $\varphi * f \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$, over an admissible class we characterize exactly: the splitting holds precisely when the modulus of continuity is dominated by the H\"older modulus of exponent $n_p - \lceil n_p \rceil + 1$ ($n_p := n(1/p - 1)$) and the decay majorant satisfies an $\ell^p$-Dini summability, iterated once more at integer $n_p$. The class is thus maximal, reaching H\"older order $n_p$ and critical decay $|x|^{-n/p}$ via a new molecular theory, with necessity shown by counterexamples on the regularity, decay, and cancellation axes; no such characterization was previously known, even at $p = 1$. Byproducts include uniform bounds for mollified atoms and molecules, coefficient conditions, quasi-norm equivalences, and unconditional $L^2$-convergence of the atomic decomposition, with an exact error identity.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed El Aoumari

item.title: A $p = 2$ dichotomy for uniform Riesz transform bounds on stratified Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2608.20267v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a stratified Lie group and $\mathcal L$ be its sub-Laplacian. We prove that the full horizontal Riesz transform $\nabla_{H} \mathcal L^{-1/2}$ is of weak type $(1,1)$ on real-valued functions, with constant at most $2$. In particular, the constant is independent of the horizontal dimension, the homogeneous dimension, the step, and the underlying group structure of $\mathbb{G}$. Our result provides a noncommutative generalization of the dimension-free Euclidean theorem of Ouyang, Spector, and Stockdale arXiv:2608.18068, with the same universal constant. Our proof relies upon a fractional obstacle problem adapted to stratified Lie groups by using the functional calculus of $\mathcal L$ instead of the Fourier transform. As a consequence, by interpolation we obtain uniform $L^p$ bounds for the full horizontal Riesz transform $\nabla_{H} \mathcal L^{-1/2}$ for $p \in (1,2]$. By contrast, for every $p > 2$, we construct a sequence of stratified Lie groups with fixed horizontal dimension $5$ and steps tending to infinity for which the $L^p$ norms of the horizontal Riesz transforms diverge.
item.dc:creator: Sheng-Chen Mao, Yaojun Wang, Ye Zhang
